title: a teaching role in the house
word: a teaching role in the house
hook: three teachers, three answers, and an Upanishad that won't vote
carry: a teaching role in the house

segments.voice: Yesterday, a lineage in the Gita: lost over time, and told again to a friend. Today the path turns from the line of teachers to the house where teaching happens.

Ask three relatives what a kid most needs to learn and you'll have three answers before dessert. Be honest. Be disciplined. Know where you come from. The Taittiriya Upanishad has its own version of that dinner table. Three named teachers, three different answers. And the text does something unusual with them.
screen: `THREE ANSWERS BEFORE DESSERT.` → `THREE NAMED TEACHERS.` → `WHAT DOES THE TEXT DO?`

segments.voice: First, the setting. The Taittiriya walks through a household, item by item. Right order, and learning and teaching. Truth, and learning and teaching. Self-control, calm, the household fires, guests, children, grandchildren, and after every one the same pair comes back: svadhyaya and pravachana, study and teaching. It sets them beside the guest at the door and the grandchild in the next room. Then the three voices. Satyavachas Rathitara says: truth. His case: without honesty, everything else in the house is built on sand. Taponitya Paurushishti says: tapas, austerity, discipline. His case: nothing learned holds without the steady effort that holds it. And Naka Maudgalya says: learning and teaching alone, for that is tapas, that is tapas. His case: study and passing it on aren't a break from discipline. They are the discipline. Notice that Naka doesn't throw out austerity. He folds it into the reading and the teaching. And the Upanishad itself keeps all three names on the page. It doesn't declare a winner. A teaching role in the house, here, belongs to whoever keeps the pair going: a little study, a little passing on, next to everything else.
screen: `STUDY AND TEACHING, AFTER EACH.` · `SATYAVACHAS: TRUTH.` · `TAPONITYA: DISCIPLINE.` · `NAKA: STUDY IS DISCIPLINE.`

segments.voice: Write three words on a scrap of paper: truth, discipline, study. Under each, write the name of someone who taught you that one, at home or anywhere. Then rest your eyes on the three names and breathe.
A teaching role in the house: study and teaching set beside every part of home life, as the Taittiriya lists them, with three teachers left standing side by side.

howItsDone: In some Hindu homes elders tell stories, teach prayers and keep a little daily reading going; the Taittiriya's list (1.9) is sometimes quoted to say study and teaching belong at home, not only at school.
